_comment: Per-army records in RAM. Base is the EWRAM pointer stored in ROM at
0x08282CBC; stride 0x68 comes from the damage path, which does
`movs r0,#0x68 ; muls r0,r6,r0` before indexing it.
The array is 1-INDEXED. Record 0 is a dummy and P1 is record 1. That is not
a guess: with P1 to move, record 1 held the on-screen funds at +00 while
records 2 and 3 held zero, and only the active player has spendable funds.
It also lines up with the terrain ownership encoding, where owner 0 is
neutral and 1..4 are the players -- so army record N owns tiles tagged N.

provenance.method: live RAM capture, offsets pinned by on-screen values

0x00.name: funds_available
0x00.note: spendable now; zero for every player whose turn it is not

0x08.name: funds_incoming
0x08.note: income shown on the status screen; equal for all players here

0x1D.name: co_related
0x1D.note: differs per CO: Andy 1, Max 2, Sami 4. Read by the damage path only when a CO power is active, where it is scaled by 292.

0x1E.name: co_modifier_index
0x1E.note: the damage path computes co*128+292 from this to reach the per-unit modifier table. Observed as 0 for Andy, Max and Sami alike.

open_questions.question: Do AW1 COs have any passive per-unit damage modifiers at all?
open_questions.detail: With no power active the damage path indexes the modifier table by +0x1E, which read 0 for Andy, Max and Sami. Table entry 0 is uniformly 100/100. Taken at face value that means no CO applies a passive damage modifier in AW1, and the 'use a neutral CO' precaution during calibration was unnecessary. But the ROM clearly contains other CO records with real modifiers (150/100, 170/100), so something must select them.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If true, calibration data is valid regardless of CO choice. If false, there is a selection mechanism we have not found.
open_questions.resolve_by: Record the same matchup twice, once with Andy and once with Max. Identical damage means no passive modifier; different damage means +0x1E is not the whole story.

open_questions.question: What is the CO id ordering at +0x1D?
open_questions.detail: Three data points: Andy 1, Max 2, Sami 4. The gap at 3 rules out a simple select-screen ordering. P4 (Olaf) was not captured.
open_questions.resolve_by: armyhex(5) to reach record 4, plus a few more CO choices.
